body: @ncw I guess it was caused by recent config patches.  Is it fixed by 1.55.1?

> @ncw I guess it was caused by recent config patches.

Yes

>  Is it fixed by 1.55.1?

Not yet!

For info: v1.54.1 also does not ask for password, so its introduced with v1.55.

Workaround is to run with option for memory-only config, although it has its own [issue](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/5222). But is there a plan for a better solution to this, avoiding the need for such option, for --version or even more generic?
Related to issue https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/5236, for which a *possible* solution described in comments will fix this one too.

#### What is the purpose of this change?

Restructuring of config code in v1.55 resulted in config file being loaded early at process startup. If configuration file is encrypted this means user will need to supply the password, even when running commands that does not use config. This also lead to an issue where mount with --deamon failed to decrypt the config file when it had to prompt user for passord.

This PR removes the forced config file loading at startup, and instead waits until first actual config access.

#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?

Fixes #5236
Fixes #5228

#### The associated forum post URL from `https://forum.rclone.org`



#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

I was detecting the version of rclone via ``rclone --version`` but since one of the last updates it tries to decrypt password protected configs which broke my very easy detection before prompting any password.

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)

1.55.1

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (e.g. Windows 7, 64 bit)

Ubuntu

#### Which cloud storage system are you using? (e.g. Google Drive)



#### The command you were trying to run (e.g. `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

``rclone --version | awk 'NR == 1 {print $2}'``

#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (e.g. output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)



#### Workaround

I figured out that I could use ``HOME=/ rclone --version 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 {print $2}'`` to workaround this.
